briefTitle: Administration of Anti-anxiety Medicine Prior to Foley Catheter Removal After HoLEP
officialTitle: A Single-Center, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial Comparing Lorazepam, Mirtazapine, and Acetaminophen Administered Prior to Foley Catheter Removal After Holmium Laser Enucleation of the Prostate (HoLEP)

arms.label: Acetaminophen (Control Arm)
arms.description: (Control Arm) Acetaminophen is a widely used analgesic and antipyretic with a well established safety profile. It is FDA approved for mild to moderate pain and is already part of a standard post-operative care regimen. Acetaminophen has no known effects on anxiety, voiding, or pelvic floor muscle tone, making it an appropriate control for this study.

arms.label: Lorazepam Arm
arms.description: Lorazepam is a short-acting benzodiazepine that acts by enhancing the effect of gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor complex. This produces anxiolytic, sedative and skeletal muscle relaxant effects. Lorazepam is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for short-term relief of anxiety symptoms associated with anxiety disorders.

arms.label: Mirtazapine Arm
arms.description: Mirtazapine is an atypical tetracyclic antidepressant FDA approved for use in major depressive disorder. It inhibits central presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic and histamine-1 receptors, leading to increased serotonin and norepinephrine release which contributes to its anxiolytic, calming and antiemetic effects.

eligibility.text:
Inclusion Criteria:

\- Individuals undergoing HoLEP for the treatment of bothersome lower urinary tract symptoms

Exclusion Criteria:

* Individuals with a known allergy or contraindication to Lorazepam, Mirtazapine or Acetaminophen
* Individuals with current chronic benzodiazepine use or history of benzodiazepine use disorder
* Severe hepatic (Child-Pugh C) or renal (eGFR \< 30mL/min) impairment
* Any intraoperative complication necessitating prolonged catheterization or ICU admission (will be unenrolled from the study)
* Planned overnight admission due to any medical or social reasons
* Individuals who are unable to take oral medications
* Individuals who lack decisional capacity
* Individuals who are unable to read/speak English
